title: Calls, texts & voice notes
goal: Make and answer calls, cope with a bad line, message and voice-note friends, share your location, and say what you've just, already or still not done.
intro:
Most of your Sindhi will happen on the phone: calls that keep cutting out, missed calls from Mum, WhatsApp groups and long voice notes from friends. This unit gives you the words for all of it — most of them English, used with Sindhi verbs (**ڪال ڪرڻ**، **ميسيج موڪلڻ**، **ڪٽجي وڃڻ**).

The grammar makes your sentences flow: the **'having done' form** (**پهچي** 'having arrived', **ڏسي** 'having seen') lets you say 'text me **when you get home**' — **گهر پهچي ميسيج ڪجانءِ** — and the little words **اڃا** 'still / yet', **پهريان ئي** 'already', **هاڻي ئي** 'just now' and **رڳو** 'only' do the rest.

grammar.title: Do X and then Y: پهچي، ڏسي، ڪري
grammar.body:
To join two actions done one after the other — 'get home **and** call', 'call **when you get** home', 'read it **and** reply' — Sindhi puts the first verb in the **'having done' form** (the conjunctive participle) and only the last verb carries the tense:

گهر **پهچي** فون ڪجانءِ — lit. 'having reached home, call' = call when you get home.

**How to make it:** verb stem + **-ي** (-ī):
ڏسڻ → **ڏسي** ɗisī · پڙهڻ → **پڙهي** paṛhī · ٻڌڻ → **ٻڌي** ɓudhī · پهچڻ → **پهچي** pahuchī · ڪرڻ → **ڪري** karī · کائڻ → **کائي** khāī · وٺڻ → **وٺي** vaṭhī · ڏيڻ → **ڏئي** ɗaī · ٿيڻ → **ٿي** thī

It never changes for person, gender or tense: مان / هوءَ / اسين … **ڏسي** …

It also covers 'when / after' and 'by doing': ماني **کائي** فون ڪندس 'I'll call after eating'; لوڪيشن **ڏسي** اچي ويندس 'I'll find it from the location'.

You've already seen the same form inside **compound verbs** (Unit 13 on): **ٿي** ويو، **اچي** وئي، **ڪٽجي** وئي.

**Trap:** don't add ۽ between the two verbs — ميسيج پڙهي ۽ جواب ڏنائين sounds clumsy; just ميسيج پڙهي جواب ڏنائين.

examples.en: I'll text you when I get to the office. (man)
I'll call you after I eat. (man)

grammar.title: Just, already, still, yet: هاڻي ئي، پهريان ئي، اڃا
grammar.body:
**اڃا** añā — **still** with a positive verb, **yet** with a negative:
مان **اڃا** آفيس ۾ آهيان 'I'm still at the office' · هن **اڃا** جواب نه ڏنو آهي 'she hasn't replied yet' · **اڃا تائين** ڪو جواب ناهي 'still no reply (up to now)'. **اڃا به** = 'even now, still': اڃا به ناراض آهين؟

**پهريان ئي** pahiryāṃ ī (or **اڳ ۾ ئي**) — **already**: مون **پهريان ئي** ٻڌايو هو 'I'd already told you'.

**هاڻي ئي** hāṇe ī — **just (now)**, with a past verb: هو **هاڻي ئي** آن لائين آيو 'he's just come online'; هاڻي ئي ڏٺم 'I've just seen it'.

**رڳو** raɠo — **only, just** (= nothing more): **رڳو** ٻه منٽ 'just two minutes'.

The particle **ئي** (ī) adds emphasis to the word before it — 'that very', 'at all': جواب **ئي** نه ڏنو 'didn't even reply'; سگنل **ئي** ڪونهي 'there's no signal at all'.

**Trap:** English 'yet' in a question ('have you eaten yet?') is usually **اڃا** + negative or simply the perfect: ماني کاڌي اٿئي؟ — not هاڻي ئي.

culture:
In Sindh, as across Pakistan, **WhatsApp is the phone**: calls, voice notes, family groups full of good-morning pictures and forwarded videos, and the endless **مسڊ ڪال** — which can mean 'call me back (I've no credit)', 'I've arrived' or 'I'm outside, come down'. Long **وائس نوٽ** are completely normal, especially from older relatives who prefer talking to typing; many people type Sindhi in Roman letters, others in the Sindhi script with a Sindhi keyboard.

Phone manners: start with **السلام عليڪم** and ask after everyone's health before getting to the point — with elders, jumping straight in sounds abrupt. If someone's parent picks up, switch to **توهان** and **جي**: **السلام عليڪم چاچا، بلال گهر ۾ آهي؟** Calls end with a round of **چڱو، ٻيو ٻڌايو** ('OK, anything else?'), **ڌيان رکجو** and **الله حافظ**, which can take a while.

Away from the cities, signal comes and goes, so **ٻڌين پيو؟** and **لائين خراب آهي** are very useful — and 'I'll call you when I reach somewhere with signal' is a perfectly good reason for silence.

tip.title: ٻڌين پيو؟ ٻڌين پئي؟ ٻڌو ٿا؟
tip.body:
- 'Can you hear me?' is literally 'are you hearing?': **ٻڌين پيو؟** (to a man) · **ٻڌين پئي؟** (to a woman) · **ٻڌو ٿا؟** (polite or to a group).
- 'I can hear you now': هاڻي **ٻڌان** ٿو / ٿي.
- Hang up = فون **رکڻ**.

tip.title: Do X and then Y: stem + ي
tip.body:
- The first action takes **-ي** and no tense: ڏسڻ → **ڏسي**, پهچڻ → **پهچي**, ڪرڻ → **ڪري**, کائڻ → **کائي**.
- Only the last verb shows who and when: گهر **پهچي** ميسيج **ڪندس**.
- It means 'and then', 'when' or 'after'. No ۽ between them.

tip.title: Still / yet / already / just
tip.body:
- **اڃا** = still; with نه = not yet: **اڃا** نه ڏٺو.
- **پهريان ئي** = already · **هاڻي ئي** = just now (with a past verb).
- **رڳو** = only, just: رڳو ٻه منٽ.
- **ئي** stresses the word before it: سگنل **ئي** ڪونهي.

tip.title: English word + Sindhi verb
tip.body:
- Most phone words are English: you add a Sindhi verb. **چارج ڪرڻ**، **ميسيج ڪرڻ**، **ڪال ڪرڻ**.
- Things that stop working **ختم ٿيڻ** (run out) or **هليو وڃڻ** (go): بيٽري ختم ٿي وئي، نيٽ هليو ويو.
- Working = **هلڻ**: نيٽ نٿو هلي.

- Keep doing = -ندا + **رهجو**: ڪال ڪندا **رهجو** 'keep calling'.
